description.narrative: Change will happen as the creative sector in target countries gain visibility and influence as a powerful driver of sustainable and inclusive growth that contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As target countries’ creative infrastructure develops, the United Kingdom (UK) creative sector will find it more attractive to build professional links and ultimately build new opportunities to work overseas.The change we make:◼Increased opportunities for women, disabled and underrepresented individuals within the cultural and creative industries.◼Evidence and insight into creative sectors will be used in countries and by the UK sector to help support development and create pathways for future market opportunities. ◼Audiences internationally have a greater engagement with, and favourability towards, UK Arts, culture and creativity.◼The UK is seen as a pioneer of the creative economy, and creative sectors overseas are strengthened. ◼The UK's Arts, Culture and Creative sectors are better connected internationally.

Creative Economy is one of the Global Programmes through which the British Council delivers its grant-funded activity. The primary focus of this Global Programme is ODA eligible activity and outcomes.This programme is based on the premise that, collectively, the cultural and creative industries can bring vast benefits in terms of economic and social value. To do this, they need to be well understood and effectively nurtured by policymakers, funders and intermediary organisations. This programme will deliver evidence and insight into creative sectors in priority countries. This data will be used in the countries themselves, and by the UK sector to help support development and create pathwaysThere are three key areas of activity: 1) Research, Insight & Advocacy 2) Sector Development, 3) Leadership and Learning.◼ 1. Research, Insight & Advocacy:◾Scoping and Research◾Convening the PEC Global Creative Economy Council ◾Contributing to Industry events◾Sharing insight with UK and international target audiences◼ 2. Sector Development:◾Targeted Sector Development Programmes ◾Delegations ◼ 3. Leadership and Learning:◾Enterprise Training ◾ Online Learning offers ◾Leadership development with Alumni

The audience for the Creative Economy programme is principally:◼Business-to-Government (B2G) to strengthen policymaking with research insight toward more equitable access, inclusion, impact and value to global, regional and countries’ creative economies.◼Business-to-Business (B2B) for sector skills development, international networks, arts enterprise and leadership.◼Artists.◼ Art sector.◼Policy makers.
